column1: # sync-log.tsv — one row per published public-mirror sync, newest LAST.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (your-org/nexus-code#979 §5). Reconstructing the mirror
# as a three-way merge is sound, but the MERGE BASE decides correctness and
# fails silently in the LEAKIER direction. The correct base is
# `scrub_old(source_old)` — the artifact the previous sync actually produced —
# and computing that requires knowing which source commit the previous sync
# shipped from. That fact lived in a report, or in somebody's memory.
# Measured on the sync this file was added for: the wrong base produced 2
# conflicts and silently carried a denied token plus 19 occurrences of a URL for
# a repository that does not exist. The right base produced 18 conflicts — the
# extra 16 being exactly the decisions that would otherwise have been made
# silently, in the direction of the older, leakier value.
# The dictionary is versioned in the same repository as the source, which is
# what makes the correct base cheap to compute: `scrub_old(source_old)` is just
# "check out source_old — dictionary and all — and run build.sh". You do not
# need to reconstruct an old dictionary by hand; you need to not accidentally
# use the CURRENT one. `sync-base.sh` does exactly that, reading the last row
# here for the sha.
# Columns (TAB-separated):
#   sync <TAB> ISO_DATE <TAB> SOURCE_SHA <TAB> MIRROR_HEAD_AFTER <TAB> NOTE
#     SOURCE_SHA         the source commit that sync was built from. This is
#                        the one `sync-base.sh` needs; get it wrong and the
#                        merge silently reverts every dictionary improvement
#                        made since.
#     MIRROR_HEAD_AFTER  the mirror commit the sync produced, so the base can
#                        be checked against what actually landed.
#     NOTE               free text; no internal identifiers (this file ships
#                        nowhere, but the habit is cheap and the cost of the
#                        exception is not).
# APPEND a row as part of every sync, before you consider it done. A sync that
# did not record itself has handed the next one a guess.
# CORRECTION (2026-09-18). The row below shipped with MIRROR_HEAD_AFTER =
# c696071, which is WRONG: c696071e is the mirror head BEFORE that sync, i.e.
# the PARENT of the commit it produced. The correct value is 7e132e36.
# How it was established: the mirror tip at the time of this correction was
# 7e132e36, and `git rev-parse 7e132e36^` is c696071e exactly -- so the
# recorded value is that commit's parent, not the commit. The SOURCE_SHA
# column (e256d4a) was NOT affected and is independently corroborated by the
# mirror commit's own subject, "Sync public mirror to dev e256d4a".
# The off-by-one entered through the row's own stated provenance -- the
# anchors were RECOVERED FROM A REPORT rather than read off the mirror. That
# provenance can recur, so it is named here rather than quietly fixed:
# a recovered anchor should be checked against the mirror before it is
# written down. Only column 4 is corrected; nothing else in the row changed.
sync
column5: first sync recorded here; anchors recovered from the sync report (MIRROR_HEAD_AFTER corrected 2026-09-18 from c696071, which was that commit's parent)
